chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The funeral prayer is performed at any hour, for it is not a prayer of bowing and prostration; rather, prayer is disliked at the rising of the sun and at its setting, which are times of bowing and prostration, because the sun sets between the horns of Satan and rises between the horns of Satan.
ai.seo_question: Can funeral prayer be performed at any time of day?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of prayer at specific times applies only to prayers involving ruku' and sujud, thereby permitting Salat al-Janazah at all hours. It highlights the jurisprudential distinction between the ritual nature of daily prayers and the funeral prayer, linking the 'krahah' (dislike) to the sun's rising and setting between the horns of Satan, a concept rooted in Shia exegesis. This ruling ensures flexibility in funeral rites while maintaining respect for the sacred times of daily worship.
